items.stem: Give two differences between organ level and organ system level.
items.answer: Organ level: tissues grouped to form organs; seen in platyhelminthes. Organ system level: complete or incomplete digestive systems differ in complexity; seen in annelids, arthropods, molluscs, echinoderms and chordates.

items.stem:
An animal has this type of circulatory system: seen in arthropods and molluscs; cells and tissues directly bathed in blood; blood pumped out through the heart.
(i) Identify the type. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were a closed circulatory system? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) An open circulatory system (ii) blood flows in open spaces (sinuses) (iii) seen in annelids and chordates; arteries, veins and capillaries present
items.markingKey: (i) an open circulatory system – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: blood flows in open spaces (sinuses) – 1 mark. (iii) for a closed circulatory system: blood circulated through a series of vessels of varying diameters; arteries, veins and capillaries present; seen in annelids and chordates – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following is a coelomate animal?

items.stem:

(b) An animal group shows these features: cells arranged as loose aggregates. Identify the level of body organisation – organ system level or cellular level? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Organ system level: organs associated to form functional systems; seen in annelids, arthropods, molluscs, echinoderms and chordates; complete or incomplete digestive systems differ in complexity. items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: cellular level; 1 mark: “cells arranged as loose aggregates” is a feature of cellular level.

items.answer: (a) An open circulatory system: blood pumped out through the heart; cells and tissues directly bathed in blood; seen in arthropods and molluscs. A closed circulatory system: blood circulated through a series of vessels of varying diameters; arteries, veins and capillaries present; seen in annelids and chordates. items.stem: Give the distinguishing features of phylum Arthropoda and phylum Mollusca, with three examples of each.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Platyhelminthes and Ctenophora on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An animal shows these characters: diploblastic and radially symmetrical. Identify its phylum – Platyhelminthes or Ctenophora? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Platyhelminthes: dorso-ventrally flattened body; flame cells; acoelomate and bilaterally symmetrical. Ctenophora: eight rows of ciliated comb plates; bioluminescence; exclusively marine. (b) Ctenophora.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: Ctenophora; 1 mark: “diploblastic and radially symmetrical” is a feature of Ctenophora.

items.stem: Define the term “coelom”.
items.answer: A body cavity lined by mesoderm.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a body cavity lined by mesoderm.

items.stem: Which of the following is a mammal?
items.answer: Balaenoptera (blue whale)
items.markingKey: (d) Balaenoptera (blue whale) is a mammal; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about phylum Chordata is incorrect?
items.answer: Amphibians have a four-chambered heart.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “Amphibians have a four-chambered heart.” Correct form: Amphibians have a three-chambered heart (two auricles, one ventricle).
options: All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.
Mammals have external ears or pinnae.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Reptiles have moist skin without scales.”
items.answer: Reptiles have dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Reptiles have dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a closed circulatory system and an open circulatory system on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An animal has this type of circulatory system: seen in arthropods and molluscs. Identify the type – a closed circulatory system or an open circulatory system? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A closed circulatory system: blood circulated through a series of vessels of varying diameters; arteries, veins and capillaries present; seen in annelids and chordates. An open circulatory system: blood pumped out through the heart; cells and tissues directly bathed in blood; seen in arthropods and molluscs. (b) An open circulatory system.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: an open circulatory system; 1 mark: “seen in arthropods and molluscs” is a feature of an open circulatory system.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the non-chordate phyla is correct?
items.answer: Coelenterates exhibit two basic body forms, polyp and medusa.
items.markingKey: (a) Coelenterates exhibit two basic body forms, polyp and medusa. The other statements are false. Sponges are generally marine; a few, like Spongilla, are fresh water. They were earlier considered a sub-phylum under phylum Chordata. Aschelminthes are dioecious; females are often longer than males.
options: Coelenterates exhibit two basic body forms, polyp and medusa.
Sponges are mostly fresh water animals.
Hemichordates were earlier placed under Annelida.

items.stem: Compare Chondrichthyes and Amphibia on any three points.
items.answer: Chondrichthyes: placoid scales; gill slits separate and without operculum; cartilaginous endoskeleton. Amphibia: tympanum represents the ear; cloaca common to alimentary, urinary and reproductive tracts; three-chambered heart.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. Chondrichthyes – placoid scales; gill slits separate and without operculum; cartilaginous endoskeleton; Amphibia – tympanum represents the ear; cloaca common to alimentary, urinary and reproductive tracts; three-chambered heart.

items.stem: Explain the term “water vascular system”.
items.answer: A system of echinoderms that helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food and respiration.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a system of echinoderms that helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food and respiration.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Platyhelminthes have a true coelom.
Reason (R): Platyhelminthes to chordates are triploblastic.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Platyhelminthes are acoelomates. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Reptilia and Amphibia on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A vertebrate has these characters: snakes and lizards shed their scales as skin cast. Identify its class – Reptilia or Amphibia? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Reptilia: dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes; usually three-chambered heart; fertilisation internal. Amphibia: moist skin without scales; tympanum represents the ear; cloaca common to alimentary, urinary and reproductive tracts. (b) Reptilia.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: Reptilia; 1 mark: “snakes and lizards shed their scales as skin cast” is a feature of Reptilia.

items.stem: An animal shows these characters: diploblastic with radial symmetry; cnidoblasts with stinging capsules. Identify its phylum. Give a reason.
items.answer: Coelenterata
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Coelenterata; 1 mark: the features diploblastic with radial symmetry; cnidoblasts with stinging capsules are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an acoelomate animal?
items.answer: Wuchereria
items.markingKey: (d) Wuchereria is a pseudocoelomate animal, not an acoelomate animal.

items.stem: Which term describes the condition in which the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane?
items.answer: bilateral symmetry
items.markingKey: (b) Bilateral symmetry: the condition in which the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Ascaris is hermaphrodite.”
items.answer: Aschelminthes are dioecious; females are often longer than males.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Aschelminthes are dioecious; females are often longer than males.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a bony fish?
items.answer: Ichthyophis (limbless amphibia)
items.markingKey: (a) Ichthyophis (limbless amphibia) is an amphibian, not a bony fish.

items.stem: An animal has this type of circulatory system: seen in annelids and chordates; blood does not bathe the tissues directly. Identify the type. Give a reason.
items.answer: A closed circulatory system
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a closed circulatory system; 1 mark: the features seen in annelids and chordates; blood does not bathe the tissues directly are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
A vertebrate has these characters: pneumatic bones; forelimbs modified into wings; feathers and a beak.
(i) Identify its class. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were Cyclostomata? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Aves (ii) crop and gizzard in the digestive tract (iii) body devoid of scales and paired fins; 6–15 pairs of gill slits
items.markingKey: (i) Aves – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: crop and gizzard in the digestive tract – 1 mark. (iii) for Cyclostomata: sucking and circular mouth without jaws; body devoid of scales and paired fins; 6–15 pairs of gill slits – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as member of Coelenterata or member of Arthropoda: Aurelia, Physalia, Meandrina, Laccifer.
items.answer: Aurelia – member of Coelenterata; Physalia – member of Coelenterata; Meandrina – member of Coelenterata; Laccifer – member of Arthropoda.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Aurelia – member of Coelenterata; Physalia – member of Coelenterata; Meandrina – member of Coelenterata; Laccifer – member of Arthropoda.

items.stem: An animal shows these characters: pseudocoelomate; sexes separate (dioecious). Identify its phylum.
items.answer: Aschelminthes
items.markingKey: (c) Aschelminthes: pseudocoelomate; sexes separate (dioecious).

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Echinodermata and Platyhelminthes on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An animal shows these characters: flame cells. Identify its phylum – Echinodermata or Platyhelminthes? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Echinodermata: calcareous ossicles in the endoskeleton; water vascular system; radially symmetrical adults. Platyhelminthes: dorso-ventrally flattened body; flame cells; acoelomate and bilaterally symmetrical. (b) Platyhelminthes.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: Platyhelminthes; 1 mark: “flame cells” is a feature of Platyhelminthes.

items.stem: Explain the term “diploblastic animals”.
items.answer: Animals in which the cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: animals in which the cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm.

items.stem: Which of the following is a reptile?
items.answer: Naja (cobra)
items.markingKey: (b) Naja (cobra) is a reptile; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about phylum Chordata is incorrect?
items.answer: All mammals are viviparous.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “All mammals are viviparous.” Correct form: Most mammals are viviparous; the platypus (Ornithorhynchus) lays eggs.
options: All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.
In Cephalochordata the notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life.
